name: Shahan ful
author: Wikibooks Cookbook contributors

ingredients.item: 2 cups dried fava beans (or canned fava beans)
2 tbsp olive oil or niter kibbeh
Yogurt or feta cheese for serving (optional)
Bread rolls or flatbread for serving

steps: Wash and soak the dried fava beans overnight.
Drain the beans and place them in a large pot with fresh water.
Simmer over low heat until the beans become soft and tender. Add more water if necessary.
Mash the cooked beans into a coarse paste using a spoon or potato masher.
In another pan, heat the olive oil or niter kibbeh over medium heat.
Add the onions and cook until soft.
Stir in the garlic, tomatoes, chilies, cumin, and berbere spice.
Cook for several minutes until fragrant.
Add the mashed beans and stir well.
Season with lemon juice, salt, and black pepper.
Simmer for a few minutes until thick.
Serve hot with yogurt, feta cheese, or fresh herbs if desired.

culture.text: Shahan ful, simplified to ful, is a dish common in Sudan, South Sudan, Somalia, Ethiopia and other parts of the Horn of Africa, which is generally served for breakfast. Believed to originate from Sudan, it is made by slowly cooking fava beans in water. Once the beans have softened, they are crushed into a coarse paste. It is often served with chopped green onions, tomatoes, and hot green peppers, as well as yogurt, feta cheese, olive oil, tesmi, berbere, lemon juice, cumin, and chili pepper. It is typically eaten without the aid of utensils accompanied with a bread roll. It is popular during the Ramadan season and during the various Lents.
